minor.orig: ...decade later. This page covers all three, framed for the urogynecologist rather than the delivering obstetrician.

minor.orig: Antenatal: digital perineal self-massage from ~34-35 weeks reduces perineal trauma requiring suture (RR 0.91, NNT ~15) and episiotomy (RR 0.84); the benefit is confined to women without prior vaginal birth, and third-/fourth-degree tears are not reduced.<sup>[2][10][18]</sup>
minor.rev: ...and episiotomy (RR 0.84).<sup>[18]</sup> The benefit is confined to women without prior vaginal birth, and third-/fourth-degree tears are not reduced.<sup>[2][10]</sup>
minor.why: Moved citation: sentence split, so [18] now supports only the RR/NNT effect figures and [2][10] only the 'confined to nulliparas / no effect on 3rd-4th degree' clause; originally all three supported the whole. Claim content unchanged, but attribution narrowed and [18] no longer on the qualifier.

minor.orig: mediolateral/lateral is preferred over midline (midline is associated with sphincter injury); during operative vaginal birth, mediolateral episiotomy reduces OASIS by ~43% with vacuum and ~68% with forceps in nulliparas.<sup>[2][10]</sup>
minor.rev: mediolateral or lateral is preferred over midline, which is associated with sphincter injury.<sup>[2]</sup> During operative vaginal birth, mediolateral episiotomy reduces OASIS by about 43% with vacuum and about 68% with forceps in nulliparas.<sup>[10]</sup>
minor.why: Moved citation: [2][10] split so [2] sits on the preference claim and [10] on the OASIS percentages; same claims, narrower attribution.

minor.orig: ...less suture removal (RR 0.56); a 2025 systematic review of 55 RCTs confirmed superiority ... no pain difference by suture material.<sup>[4][5]</sup>
minor.rev: ...less suture removal (RR 0.56).<sup>[4]</sup> A 2025 systematic review of 55 RCTs confirmed superiority ... by suture material.<sup>[5]</sup>
minor.why: Moved citation: [4] now on the Cochrane meta-analysis clause, [5] on the 2025 SR clause; matches the described sources, same claims.

minor.orig: Sequelae bullets with arrows ('Prolapse - via levator avulsion ... -> links')
minor.why: Arrow shorthand converted to verbs ('arises', 'results from', 'is used for'); mildly more assertive causal wording, but original 'via'/'from' already implied causation.

notes: No numbers, hedges, populations or trial names changed. Five citation moves (antenatal massage, episiotomy, continuous repair, perineorrhaphy, plus split of intrapartum untouched) are all splits of a multi-ref cluster onto the sub-clauses each plausibly supports; none attaches a citation to a claim different in substance, so all classed minor. The antenatal move is the most notable since [18] is dropped from the qualifier and [2][10] from the effect sizes. MDX intact; em-dashes and bold removed.
